cases.description: Reflection hero-image request gets the documented workaround, not silent rule-breaking
cases.request: My hero image is the character seen in a mirror — build the scene around it
cases.response:
Routing to higgsfield-seedance (high-risk shot type: reflections — ENGINE-RULES.md rule 8).

Seedance breaks scene geography rendering reflector + reflected together, so we flag this rather than prompt it directly. Workaround: shoot the reflection **as** the scene — pin your mirror image as the start frame of its own dedicated reflection-frame composition, then cut (double-contrast) to the physical subject in a separate beat. Never show the mirror and the subject in one continuous beat.

cases.description: Exit-frame = implicit cut respected in multi-beat prompts
cases.request: Character walks out of frame then comes back
cases.response:
Routing to higgsfield-seedance (exit-frame = implicit cut — ENGINE-RULES.md rule 6).

A character who leaves frame is gone for the remainder of that continuous beat — exit + re-entry in one beat is unpromptable. Structure it as two beats instead: beat one ends on the exit; beat two re-anchors position and facing direction after a double-contrast cut.

cases.description: ZH house-format guidance quotes the 1,800-char cap
cases.request: 我要一个中文的 Seedance 提示词，注意长度限制
cases.response:
Routing to higgsfield-seedance (ZH-house profile — ENGINE-RULES.md core applies).

中文提示词硬上限 **1,800 字符**。超限时按以下顺序裁剪：叙事概要 → 静态描述 → 风格与氛围（至少保留一句）→ 动态描述（永不整段删除）。六要素结构不变：镜头 + 主体 + 动作 + 场景 + 风格 + 光线。

cases.description: Delivered prompts come with the preflight command
cases.request: Final check before I spend credits?
cases.response:
Routing to higgsfield-seedance (pre-flight linter).

Run the full preflight before generating:

python3 scripts/seedance_lint.py --preflight --model seedance_2_0 "<your prompt>"

It chains the filter lint, the structural lint (shot counts, beat sums, enum legality from specs/model-specs.json), and a learning-memory recall into one PASS/WARN/FAIL report. Treat FAIL as do-not-generate.

cases.description: Draft-tier answer names what persists vs what re-rolls
cases.request: My 480p draft was perfect — will the 1080p version look the same?
cases.response:
Routing to higgsfield-seedance (§ Drafts Validate the Prompt, Not the Take).

Not the same take — no seed parameter means the 1080p run is a fresh roll. What carries over is everything prompt-driven: shot count, blocking, identity, dialogue placement, filter pass. What re-rolls: the performance, camera micro-trajectory, beat timing. Pin the draft's best frame as a start/end reference (Hero Frame) to carry the look, and re-check fine detail at final resolution.

cases.description: Extend-a-clip request uses the extension prompting pattern (v3.19.0)
cases.request: I have a 10s 1080p Seedance clip of a woman running down a hallway. Extend it — what happens next?
cases.response:
Routing to higgsfield-seedance (§ Extension Prompting) + higgsfield-pipeline (§ Continuation & Extension Handoff).

**Model**: Seedance 2.0
**Aspect ratio**: 16:9  **Duration**: 10s  **Resolution**: 1080p (mode=std) — match the source clip's resolution AND duration, or the model starts inventing.

Attach the existing clip as a video reference (`video_references` role), then open the prompt with:

```
The scene continues. The woman bursts through the door at the end of the hallway into a stairwell, takes the stairs two at a time, one continuous handheld shot following behind her. The scene is continuous, no scene cuts. No music.
```

If an identity detail was hidden at the source's end (face turned away), add her character image as a second reference and bind it: "The woman's identity is @Image1." Keep extension chains short — quality drifts by the ~4th–5th chained generation; cap seamless chains at 2 and re-anchor from the ORIGINAL references [FIELD]. Ending on a camera-angle change makes the join read as intentional coverage [EMPIRICAL].

cases.description: A staging diagram is sold as what it measured to be — safe, not a blocking lock — attached last, never in the first-frame role, backed by prose blocking (house-rulings P2-11)
cases.request: Can I attach a diagram to lock where my three characters stand in a Seedance shot?
cases.response:
Routing to higgsfield-seedance (§ Spatial Layout Block) + templates/seedance/staging-reference.md.

You can attach one, but not to lock positions. A staging reference — thin, muted outline figures drawn front-on from the camera's side, no fills, no letters — was measured here: it does not reliably move the blocking (renders tracked the map's orientation 6/12, which is chance), and it is safe (0/18 bleed) when all three anti-bleed layers are in place.

How to use it:

1. Attach the location and character references first and the staging reference last, as a position reference only.
2. Never give it the first-frame role — a drawing there becomes frame one.
3. Never name the map's graphic style in the video prompt, not even negated.
4. Put the positions that must hold into a written Spatial Layout Block — screen position, depth layer, orientation, contact points for all three — because the prose is what carries the blocking.

cases.description: Three individually-legal 6 s audio references exceed the measured ≤15.2 s TOTAL cap on Seedance 2.0 — and the answer states the measurement is third-party / unverified on Higgsfield
cases.request: I want to attach three 6-second MP3 clips as audio references to one Seedance 2.0 generation. Each is under the 15-second limit, so that's fine, right?
cases.response:
Routing to higgsfield-audio (§ Audio by Model → Seedance 2.0) + higgsfield-seedance.

Probably not. Each clip is legal on its own (per-clip bounds 1.8–15.2 s), but the total across all attached audio clips was measured capped at ≤15.2 s — three 6 s clips come to 18 s, and in that measurement they were rejected with a 400. It is a third-party measurement on the China Ark lane; Higgsfield's own enforcement is unverified, so if the attach fails, the total cap is the first suspect.

Keep the total at or under 15.2 s: trim to three 5 s clips (15 s), or drop one clip. MP3 only — WAV and AAC fail silently.
